title: Pawns: Convert the Last Promotion
summary: Distinguish reaching a queen from proving the win: keep every defending pawn on the board and use concrete captures to establish the conversion.

nodes.question: How should White continue the promotion plan?
nodes.explanation: e8=Q creates a queen against bishop and four pawns. That is eight pieces, so the narrated advantage needs an independently checked conversion. The saved finite strategy covers all eighteen Black replies.

branches.title: Independent king reply: win c6 with check
commentary: Begin after the bishop has moved to b6, with the white pawn on e7. Earlier sacrifices are source context rather than a certified full solution.
e8=Q promotes without check. Bb6, c6, d5, g5 and h5 remain alongside Kd3.
Kc4 is an independently supplied reply that approaches the queenside but leaves c6 exposed.
Qxc6+ removes the c-pawn and checks Kc4 down the c-file. Kh1/Qc6 against Kc4/Bb6/d5/g5/h5 is a complete seven-piece exact White win.

branches.title: Independent pawn reply: collect the exposed pawn
commentary: Compare Black advancing the g-pawn rather than moving its king. The pawn begins on g5 in this source version.
e8=Q creates the queen while retaining the full board for analysis.
g4 advances the black pawn closer to promotion but does not protect c6 or check White’s king on h1.
Qxc6 captures the c-pawn. The queen on c6 does not check Kd3; Bb6/d5/g4/h5 remain, and this complete seven-piece position is an exact White win.

branches.title: Independent bishop reply: retain the full ending
commentary: Compare a bishop retreat on the b6–c5–d4–e3 diagonal. This reply and continuation are independent analysis.
e8=Q is the source promotion; it does not remove Black’s bishop or any pawn.
Be3 relocates the bishop while retaining Kd3/c6/d5/g5/h5. No narrated general comparison of bishop and knight proves this exact ending.
Qxc6 removes the exposed c-pawn. Kh1/Qc6 against Kd3/Be3/d5/g5/h5 is an exact seven-piece White win, with all other pawns retained.

exercises.prompt: Why verify this separately from Beautiful Move Alert?
exercises.answer: The bishop is on b6 and the g-pawn is on g5. Those different squares change legal checks, captures and defenses, so the other clip’s proof cannot simply be reused.

exercises.prompt: What can we conclude about the earlier knight sacrifice?
exercises.answer: It explains the source’s promotion plan, but this study proves only the reconstructed later diagram and selected continuations. The larger knight and a-pawn variations still need their own outcome analysis.
